texts.preamble: Praveen vs Annu on 15 July, 2025 In The Court Of Ms. Sheetal Chaudhary Pradhan Addl. Sessions Judge-02, South-East District Saket Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal No. 74/2025 Ps- Sarita Vihar U/Sec. 29 Pwdv Act In the matter of :- Praveen S/o Late Sh. Ram Niwas R/o H. No. 650/32A Mehla Mohalla, Madanpur Khadar New Delhi- 110076. .... Appellant Versus Annu W/o Sh. Praveen R / o H. No. 650/32A Mehla Mohalla, Madanpur Khadar New Delhi- 110076. .... Respondent Date of Institution : 12.03.2025 Date of Arguments : 04.07.2025 Date of pronouncement : 15.07.2025 Decision : [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Impugned Order Stands Upheld. Ca No. 74/2025 Praveen Vs. Annu Page no. 1 Judgment
texts.facts: 2. Vide impugned order dated 04.02.2025, Ld. Trial Court has modified its earlier order dated 31.08.2022 vide which appellant/ husband was directed to pay a sum of Rs. 13,300/- per month to the complainant for the maintenance of the complainant as well as three minor children from the date of filing of the application till its disposal. Further, vide aforesaid impugned order, considering the income of wife/ complainant, the appellant/ husband was directed to contribute only Rs.5000/- per month (in total) towards the maintenance of three minor children from the date of filing of application i.e. 10.04.2024 and directed that remaining amount shall be contributed by the complainant. 3. Appellant/ husband herein was the respondent before Ld. Trial Court and respondent/ wife herein was the complainant before Ld. Trial Court. The brief facts necessary for disposal of present appeal as mentioned in appeal are as follows :- "That marriage of the complainant and respondent was solemnized on 25.11.2007 according to the Hindu rites and customs, at Delhi. Out of the said wedlock, three children were born out who were presently in the custody of complainant. That parents of the complainant have spent huge amount in the said marriage beyond their capacity and as per the demand of the respondent for the happiness of complainant. After the marriage, the complainant was dutiful and never gave any chance to complaint but after sometime, the behaviour of respondents have changed towards the complainant was being harassed for not bringing the dowry articles as per their whims and also demanded Rs. 10 Lacs, One Flat and Car. Thereafter, due to non- fulfillment of the said demand respondents tortured her physically as well as mentally. That respondent/ husband has extra marital affairs and alcoholic person and upon objection, complainant was beaten by him. That respondent/ husband is well educated and is earning handsomely. That a police complaint was made by the complainant but the matter was got settled with a written apology tendered by the respondents. That the matrimonial house is built up and having 33 built up rooms, apart form the two rooms in which the deponent is residing with her three minor school going children. Since, the complainant was subjected to the physical, verbal and emotional abuse as well as the economic abuse committed by the respondents, hence, the present complaint case." CA No. 74/2025 Praveen Vs. Annu Page no. 3 of 16 5. And thereafter, matter was fixed for Complainant Evidence. 6. Thereafter, cross-examination of CW1/ Complainant was got done on 20.09.2023, 05.01.2024, 10.04.2024 and 22.07.2024 and an application for modification of aforesaid order dated 31.08.2022 was filed by the respondent/ husband which was disposed off vide order dated 04.02.2025 by Ld. Trial Court by modifying its order dated 31.08.2022. And Ld. Trial Court considering the income of wife/ complainant has directed respondent/ husband to contribute only Rs.5000/- per month (in total) towards the maintenance of three minor children from the date of filing of application i.e. 10.04.2024 and directed that remaining amount shall be contributed by the complainant. 7. Feeling aggrieved by the impugned order dated 04.02.2025 passed by Ld. Trial Court, respondent/ husband has challenged the said order by way of present appeal on the following grounds :- a) That impugned order dated 04.02.2025 has been passed without applying the judicial mind and ignoring the facts came before the Court. CA No. 74/2025 Praveen Vs. Annu Page no. 4 of 16 b) That Ld. Trial Court ignored that respondent is raising some facts about maintenance being paid to complainant from the beginning and even raised during interim argument but court has relied on false averment of complainant and passed interim order dated 31.08.2022. c) That Ld. Trial Court has wrongly interpreted maintenance paid by appellant as income of the respondent/complainant as complainant was allowed to collect rent of 11 room to maintain herself and her children. Later on, Ld. Trial Court came to know that complainant is collecting the rent of 11 rooms and as per complainant is getting CA No. 74/2025 Praveen vs Annu on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80031773/ 3 Praveen Vs. Annu Page no. 5 of 16 collection of rent of Rs. 20,000/- to Rs. 25,000/- which is more than awarded amount. But Ld. Trial Court vide impugned order still imposing Rs. 5000/- per month and not whispered about the amount awarded till the date of application of u/s 25(2) filed by the respondent.
texts.arguments: 8. In addition to the aforesaid grounds, Ld. Counsel for complainant/ appellant has argued that Ld. Trial Court has erred in justifying the awarded amount i.e firstly awarded Rs. 13,300/- which was after considering the all aspect that complainant is residing with children in own house of respondent and all children are in government school. It has been argued that since the complainant is financially sound, therefore, the amount awarded vide impugned order, be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 9. On other hand, Ld. Counsel for the complainant has argued that the present appeal is devoid of merit and is liable to dismissed. It has been argued that respondent/ husband being aggrieved by the order dated 31.08.2022 filed an appeal bearing CA No. 250/2022 before the Court of Sh. Gaurav Gupta, Ld. ASJ-09 (south-East), Saket Courts, New Delhi which was dismissed vide its order dated 19.01.2023. That the present appeal filed by the respondent/ husband is the blatant abuse of the process of law and instead of making payment of interim maintenance to the respondent and her three minor children, the respondent/ husband is filing a number of cases to avoid the payment to the complainant. That rooms in the house of the respondent/ husband have been distributed by his father between the family members and further the rooms have no basic amenities like separate bathroom and kitchen etc. It has been argued that rent of the rooms is around Rs.1500/- and not Rs. 5,500/- as allegedly claimed by the respondent/ husband. It has been argued that complainant was harassed and tortured by respondent/ husband and also the sister of complainant was harassed and molested by the father of the respondent/ husband, so an FIR under relevant sections of IPC was registered against him. It has been argued CA No. 74/2025 Praveen Vs. Annu Page no. 6 of 16 that respondent was arrested by the Faridabad police and was under custody in the case of immoral trafficking and remained in jail for considerable period of time. It has been argued that complainant has three school going children viz. two girl child and one boy who needs constant care and attention and the eldest daughter of the complainant has been suffering from anxiety and depression for which she is under going treatment and counseling in private hospitals regularly, therefore, all the expenditure on the medicines and counseling is born by the complainant but on the other hand, respondent/ husband is living a lavish life and least bothered about the complainant and her children. It has been argued that the grounds of appeal are vague and present appeal is liable to be dismissed. 11. Section 20 of the DV Act stipulates that a Magistrate hearing an application under Section 12 of the DV Act may direct Respondent to pay certain monetary relief to the aggrieved person. For the ease of comprehension, Section 20 of the DV Act has been reproduced as under :- CA No. 74/2025 Praveen Vs. Annu Page no. 7 of 16 "20. Monetary reliefs Praveen vs Annu on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80031773/ 4 (1)While disposing of an application under sub-section (1) of section 12, the Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence and such relief may include, but not limited to, (a)the loss of earnings; (b)the medical expenses; (c)the loss caused due to the destruction, damage or removal of any property from the control of the aggrieved person; and (d)the maintenance for the aggrieved person as well as her children, if any, including an order under or in addition to an order of maintenance under section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974) or any other law for the time being in force. (2)The monetary relief granted under this section shall be adequate, fair and reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed." 12. 13. The Act inter-alia provides for more effective protection or the right of woman guaranteed under the constitution who are victims of the domestic violence of any kind occurring within the shared household. According to the Act, any harm, injury to health, safety, life, limb or well being or any other act or threatening or coercion etc. by any adult member of the family, constitutes domestic violence. Further, the act also contemplates that any woman who is or has been in a domestic Praveen vs Annu on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80031773/ 5 relationship, if she is subjected to any domestic violence can file a CA No. 74/2025 Praveen Vs. Annu Page no. 9 of 16 complaint u/sec. 12 of the PWDV Act. This Act also covers those woman who are or have been in relationship with the abuser where both parties have live together in a shared household and a relative by consanguinity, marriage or through a relationship in the nature of marriage or adoption. 15. For computing the maintenance, the following test have been laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Jasbir Kaur Sehgal vs. District Judge, Dehradun & Ors. 1997 (7) SCC 7, wherein it has been observed that: "No set formula can be laid for fixing the amount of maintenance. It has, in the very nature of things, to depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. Some scope for leverage can, however, be always there. The court has to consider the status of parties, their CA No. 74/2025 Praveen Vs. Annu Page no. 10 of 16 respective needs, the capacity of husband to pay having regard to his reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and of those he is obliged under the law and statutory but involuntary payments or deductions. The amount of maintenance fixed for wife or children should be such as she can live in reasonable comfort considering her status and the mode of life she was used to when she lived with her husband and also that she does not feel handicapped in the prosecution of her case. At the same time, the amount so fixed cannot be excessive or extortionate." 16. Further, Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr, Crl. Appeal No. 730/2020 (arising out of SLP (Crl) No. 9503/2018, dated 04.11.2020 has held as under :- Criteria for determining quantum of maintenance :- The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse. There is no straitjacket formula for fixing the quantum of maintenance to be awarded. The factors which would weigh with the Court inter alia are the status of the parties; reasonable needs of the wife and dependent children; whether the applicant is educated and professionally qualified; whether the applicant has any independent source of Praveen vs Annu on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80031773/ 6 income; whether the income is sufficient to enable her to maintain the same standard of living as she was accustomed to in her matrimonial home; whether the applicant was employed prior to her marriage; whether she was working during the subsistence of CA No. 74/2025 Praveen Vs. Annu Page no. 11 of 16 the marriage; whether the wife was required to sacrifice her employment opportunities for nurturing the family, child rearing, and looking after adult members of the family; reasonable costs of litigation for a nonworking wife. 17. Besides that, the court must take into consideration the status of the parties and the capacity of the spouse to pay for her or her child or his support, the financial capacity of the husband, his actual income, reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and dependent family members including his own child, whom he is obliged to maintain under the law, liabilities if any, would be required to be taken into consideration. The Court must have due regard to the standard of living of the husband, as well as the spiraling inflation rates and high costs of living. The plea of the husband that he does not possess any such source of income through which, he could maintain her wife, ipso facto does not absolve him of his moral duty to maintain his wife or his child if he is able bodied and has educational qualifications. 18. Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Rajnesh Vs Neha & Anr (Supra) has held as under :- (c) Where wife is earning some income. The Courts have held that if the wife is earning, it cannot operate as a bar from being awarded maintenance by the husband. The Courts have provided guidance on this issue in the following judgments. CA No. 74/2025 Praveen Vs. Annu Page no. 12 of 16 19. Further, in order to determine the quantum of maintenance payable to an applicant, the Court shall take into account the criteria enumerated in Part B - III of the judgment Rajnesh Vs Neha and Anr. (supra). The objective of granting interim / permanent alimony is to ensure that the dependent spouse is not reduced to destitution or vagrancy on account of the failure of the marriage, and not as a punishment to the other spouse. Under section 20 DV Act, the magistrate has powers to direct husband to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence and such relief may inter alia include the maintenance for aggrieved person as well as her children. 21. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case law titled as Dr. Kulbhushan Kunwar v. Raj Kumari (1970) 3 SCC 129, has held, which as under :- Praveen vs Annu on 15 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80031773/ 7 " 12. Section 125 Cr.P.C. stipulates that if any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain his wife, his legitimate or illegitimate minor child, who are otherwise unable to maintain themselves, shall be obligated to do so. A moral duty and a statutory obligation is cast upon the husband to maintain his wife, minor children, parents who otherwise are not capable of maintaining themselves.
